info.title: awork API
info.description: This is the API documentation for awork.

get.summary: Returns all absence regions.
get.description:
Returns all absence regions with their public holiday details.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `user-planning-data:write` permission to see users assigned to absence regions.</Check>

post.summary: Creates an absence region.
post.description:
Creates an absence region for an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country and location. Names must be unique. Marking the new region as default clears the previous default region. This operation requires a Standard workspace plan or higher.

<Note title="Subscription Level" icon="layer-group">This endpoint requires the `Standard` plan or higher.</Note>

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `user-planning-data:write` permissions.</Check>

requestBody.description: The model to create the absence region.

get.summary: Returns supported absence region countries.
get.description:
Returns the supported countries and their ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes for absence regions.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

get.summary: Returns locations for the specified country.
get.description:
Returns the country's locations as ISO 3166-2 codes, including regions and subregions when available. An unsupported country code returns not found.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

post.summary: Sets the current user's absence region.
post.description:
Sets the current user's absence region. A user can have only one region; assigning a new region replaces the previous one. A null region id removes the current assignment.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `user-planning-data:write` permissions.</Check>

requestBody.description: The model to assign or unassign the current user to/from an absence region.

put.summary: Sets the current user's absence region.
put.description:
Sets the current user's absence region. A user can have only one region; assigning a new region replaces the previous one. A null region id removes the current assignment.
            This endpoint is deprecated; use the POST endpoint instead.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `user-planning-data:write` permissions.</Check>

requestBody.description: The model to assign or unassign the current user to/from an absence region.

post.summary: Sets users for an absence region.
post.description:
Sets the users assigned to an absence region. A user can belong to only one region, so assigning a user here removes any previous assignment. An empty user list removes all assignments.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `user-planning-data:write` permissions.</Check>

requestBody.description: The model to assign or unassign users to/from an absence region.

put.summary: Sets users for an absence region.
put.description:
Sets the users assigned to an absence region. A user can belong to only one region, so assigning a user here removes any previous assignment. An empty user list removes all assignments.
            This endpoint is deprecated; use the POST endpoint instead.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `user-planning-data:write` permissions.</Check>

requestBody.description: The model to assign or unassign users to/from an absence region.

delete.summary: Deletes the specified absence region.
delete.description:
Deletes the specified absence region, unassigns its users, and deletes related workspace absences. Deleting the default region leaves the workspace without a default region.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `user-planning-data:write` permissions.</Check>

parameters.name: absenceRegionId
parameters.description: The id of the absence region to delete.

get.summary: Returns the specified absence region.
get.description:
Returns the absence region with public holiday details for its country and location.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `user-planning-data:write` permission to see users assigned to the absence region.</Check>

parameters.name: absenceRegionId
parameters.description: The id of the absence region.

put.summary: Updates the specified absence region.
put.description:
Updates the region name, country, location, or default status. Names must remain unique, and marking this region as default clears the previous default region.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `user-planning-data:write` permissions.</Check>

parameters.name: absenceRegionId
parameters.description: The id of the absence region to update.

requestBody.description: The model to update the absence region.

get.summary: Returns all absences.
get.description:
Returns workspace absences visible to the current user.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `user-planning-data:read` permission to view other users' absences.</Check>

post.summary: Creates an absence.
post.description:
Creates an absence with dates rounded to 00:00:00, 12:00:00, or 23:59:59 UTC to support full-day and half-day periods. The end date must be the same as or later than the start date, and overlapping absences are rejected unless the provider allows them.
            
             <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must own the absence, be an admin, or have `user-planning-data:write` permission.</Check>

requestBody.description: The model to create the absence.

delete.summary: Deletes the specified absence.
delete.description:
Deletes the specified absence unless it is managed by an external provider. Web and mobile requests cannot delete externally managed absences.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must own the absence, be an admin, or have `user-planning-data:delete` permission.</Check>

parameters.name: absenceId
parameters.description: The id of the absence to delete.

get.summary: Returns the specified absence.
get.description:
Returns the specified absence when it is visible to the current user.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must own the absence, be an admin, or have `user-planning-data:read` permission.</Check>

put.summary: Updates the specified absence.
put.description:
Updates the specified absence with dates rounded to 00:00:00, 12:00:00, or 23:59:59 UTC to support full-day and half-day periods. The end date must be the same as or later than the start date, and overlapping absences are rejected unless the provider allows them.
            
             Web and mobile requests cannot update absences managed by an external provider.
             <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must own the absence, be an admin, or have `user-planning-data:write` permission.</Check>

parameters.name: absenceId
parameters.description: The id of the absence to update.

requestBody.description: The model to update the absence.

delete.summary: Revokes the current account's authorizations and refresh tokens for all third-party OAuth client applications.
delete.description: <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

get.summary: Returns the third-party OAuth client applications authorized by the current account.
get.description: <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

delete.summary: Revokes the current account's authorization and refresh tokens for one third-party OAuth client application.
delete.description: <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

put.summary: Updates the account profile and starts email verification when required.
put.description: <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

requestBody.description: The model value.

post.summary: Checks a password or passwordless token for the requested account.
post.description: <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin.</Check>

parameters.name: aw-internal-request
parameters.description: Marks this request as an internal request. Only allowed by the awork app or internally.

requestBody.description: The password value.

get.summary: Returns all custom agents.
get.description:
Lists custom agents visible to the requesting user in the current workspace, including visible global agents.
            Results are ordered by name and include the user's access level for each agent.
            Use an agent id from this response to retrieve or update its configuration.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

post.summary: Creates a new custom agent.
post.description:
Creates a custom agent in the current workspace and returns its configuration and id.
            Provide a name and either PresetKey or both ModelProvider and ModelName. Do not combine these model selection options.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

requestBody.description: The configuration for the new agent.

get.summary: Lists the connectors visible to the requesting user in the current workspace.
get.description:
Lists connectors visible to the requesting user in the current workspace.
            Use the returned connector ids to link existing connectors to custom agents.
            The user must have access to the custom-agent feature.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

get.summary: Lists the predefined connector presets available to the workspace.
get.description:
Lists predefined connector presets and the OAuth callback URI used for connector setup.
            Create connectors in the awork app.
            The response describes setup options; it does not create a connector.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

parameters.name: includeAdded
parameters.description: Whether to include providers already added to the workspace for metadata lookup.

put.summary: Makes a custom connector workspace-visible or private.
put.description:
Updates whether a custom connector is visible to the workspace or private and returns its sharing configuration.
            Set IsSharedWithWorkspace to the desired visibility. Making a connector private fails while connections remain shared or another user has a connection or agent using it.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must own the connector or be a workspace administrator, and must have permission to contribute to the agent library.</Check>

requestBody.description: The connector sharing configuration.

get.summary: Gets the default agent options for a personal or custom agent.
get.description:
Returns default model, tool access, connector, and skill options for a personal-agent or custom-agent conversation.
            Set type to 'personal-agent' for the requesting user's defaults, or 'custom-agent' and provide agentId for a custom agent.
            The response also includes the effective model catalog for the workspace.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have read access to the selected custom agent.</Check>

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The agent type to resolve defaults for ('personal-agent' or 'custom-agent').

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: The id of the custom agent when  is 'custom-agent'.

get.summary: Returns thread metadata for usage analytics.
get.description:
Returns thread metadata for usage analytics, including the thread Id, name, credits, and creation timestamp.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin.</Check>

get.summary: Returns the AI models available to agents.
get.description:
Returns the agent model catalog with effective availability for the current workspace.
            The response includes model providers, model details, defaults, and available image capabilities.
            Use these values when selecting a model for an agent or conversation.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

post.summary: Disables a model, vendor, or region and updates settings that use it.
post.description:
Disables a model, vendor, or region for the workspace and updates settings that use it.
            Use the model settings in the awork app to review affected configurations and eligible replacements before disabling.
            Specify the required replacement models in the request. Returns no content when the changes are saved.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `workspace-manage-config:write` permissions.</Check>

requestBody.description: The disable and migration command.

put.summary: Sets a workspace preset to Auto or a selected active text model.
put.description:
Updates a workspace model preset to use central Auto selection or an explicit active text model.
            Identify the preset by its catalog key and provide the assignment in the request body.
            Returns no content when the assignment is saved, or a validation error if the selection is invalid.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `workspace-manage-config:write` permissions.</Check>

requestBody.description: The preset assignment.

post.summary: Enables an AI model region for the workspace.
post.description:
Enables an AI model serving region in the workspace's model policy.
            Use the stable region key from the model catalog. Returns no content when the policy is saved.
            Read [GET /agents/models](#/AgentRuntime/GetModels) to inspect the resulting model availability.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `workspace-manage-config:write` permissions.</Check>

post.summary: Enables one AI model vendor for the workspace.
post.description:
Enables an AI model vendor in the workspace's model policy.
            Use the stable vendor key from the model catalog. Returns no content when the policy is saved.
            Read [GET /agents/models](#/AgentRuntime/GetModels) to inspect the resulting model availability.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `workspace-manage-config:write` permissions.</Check>

post.summary: Enables one AI model for the workspace.
post.description:
Enables one catalog model for the workspace and returns no content when the policy is saved.
            Use the stable model key from [GET /agents/models](#/AgentRuntime/GetModels). The model's vendor and serving region must be enabled first.
            Removed models and models that cannot be changed in the current rollout state return a validation error.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `workspace-manage-config:write` permissions.</Check>

get.summary: Lists project schedules.
get.description:
Lists readable schedules directly linked to a project or linked through one of its tasks.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

get.summary: Lists owned schedules.
get.description:
Lists schedules owned by the requesting user whose active agents remain readable. The overview processes the newest 1,000 owned schedules.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

get.summary: Lists accessible skills.
get.description:
Returns one page of shared skills available to the requesting user. Pages contain at most 1000 skills. Use page and pageSize query parameters; pagination metadata is returned in aw-* headers.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

post.summary: Creates a reusable skill.
post.description:
Creates a user-owned skill and enables it when the creator may configure the awork Agent.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

requestBody.description: The request payload.

post.summary: Imports a skill package.
post.description:
Imports a skill from an agentskills.io ZIP package or standalone SKILL.md file. Pass agentId to import the skill as private to that agent; omit it to create a reusable skill.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

file.description: An agentskills.io ZIP package or standalone SKILL.md file.

content.description: Standalone SKILL.md content used by agent and MCP callers.

fileName.description: The file name used when content is supplied, for example SKILL.md.

schema.description: Upload either file or content. When content is used, fileName must identify the imported file.

delete.summary: Deletes a skill secret value.
delete.description:
Deletes a stored skill secret value. Workspace-scoped values require admin permissions; user-scoped values affect only the requesting user.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

parameters.name: envVarName
parameters.description: The env var name of the value.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: The scope of the value ("workspace" or "user").

get.summary: Lists skill secret statuses.
get.description:
Lists which secrets have saved values for the workspace or the requesting user. The secret values themselves are never returned.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

put.summary: Sets a skill secret value.
put.description:
Sets a skill secret value. Workspace-scoped values require admin permissions; user-scoped values are stored for the requesting user only.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

requestBody.description: The request payload.

delete.summary: Deletes a skill.
delete.description:
Deletes a shared skill when the caller has manage access.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

get.summary: Gets an accessible skill.
get.description:
Returns one skill when the caller has read access directly or through the optional linked agent.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: The optional linked agent through which read access is requested.

put.summary: Updates a skill.
put.description:
Updates a shared skill when the caller has manage access.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

requestBody.description: The request payload.

get.summary: Exports a skill package.
get.description:
Exports a skill as an agentskills.io ZIP package containing SKILL.md and bundled files.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: The optional linked agent through which read access is requested.

delete.summary: Deletes a skill file.
delete.description:
Deletes one bundled file by its path relative to the skill root.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

parameters.name: relativePath
parameters.description: The path of the file relative to the skill root.

get.summary: Lists skill files.
get.description:
Returns the bundled files for a skill after checking read access directly or through the optional linked agent.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: The optional linked agent through which read access is requested.

post.summary: Uploads a skill file.
post.description:
Uploads or replaces a bundled file. The relative path defaults to the uploaded file name and can be overridden with the relativePath query parameter, for example scripts/sync.py.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

parameters.name: relativePath
parameters.description: The optional target path relative to the skill root.

file.description: The bundled skill file to upload.

get.summary: Downloads a skill file.
get.description:
Downloads one bundled file by its path relative to the skill root after checking read access.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

parameters.name: relativePath
parameters.description: The path of the file relative to the skill root.

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: The optional linked agent through which read access is requested.

get.summary: Lists skill secret requirements.
get.description:
Lists the secrets a skill needs and whether they are set for the user. Secret values are never returned.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: The optional linked agent through which read access is requested.

put.summary: Updates skill secret requirements.
put.description:
Replaces the list of secrets a skill needs and returns the resulting requirements.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

requestBody.description: The request payload.

get.summary: Gets skill sharing.
get.description:
Gets the sharing configuration for a manageable, user-owned skill.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

put.summary: Updates skill sharing.
put.description:
Replaces the sharing configuration for a manageable, user-owned skill.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

requestBody.description: The replacement sharing configuration.

post.summary: Creates a conversation with the awork Agent or a custom agent.
post.description:
Creates a conversation with the awork Agent or a custom agent and optionally submits the first message.
            Supply content or attachments to submit the first message and start processing.
            awork Agent threads can be created without a message. Custom Agent threads require text or an attachment.
            The response contains the thread and accepted first-message identifiers, not the agent's reply.
            See [GET /agents/threads/{threadId}/messages](api:GET/agents/threads/{threadId}/messages) to retrieve replies.
            Each request creates a new thread. Retrying after a lost response can create another thread.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

requestBody.description: The thread creation payload.

get.summary: Gets an agent thread.
get.description:
Returns details of the specified agent conversation.
            Use the thread id returned when creating a conversation. Retrieve its messages separately with [GET /agents/threads/{threadId}/messages](api:GET/agents/threads/{threadId}/messages).
            Returns not found if the thread is missing or is not visible to the user.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.description: The id of the thread to retrieve.

post.summary: Cancels the active run for the specified agent thread.
post.description:
Cancels the active run in the specified personal-agent or custom-agent conversation and returns the thread.
            A successful cancellation also pauses dispatch of the next queued message.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have permission to contribute to the thread.</Check>

get.summary: Returns a file of the specified agent thread.
get.description:
Returns file metadata for a file attached to the specified agent thread.
            Both the thread id and file id must match the attachment. Returns not found if the file is not attached to that thread.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have `read` access to the agent thread.</Check>

get.summary: Returns content from a file attached to the specified agent thread.
get.description:
Returns the binary content of a file attached to the specified agent thread.
            Use the thread id and file id from the attachment metadata. For images, width, height, and crop control resizing.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have read access to the agent thread.</Check>

parameters.name: crop
parameters.description: Whether to crop the image when resizing it.

get.summary: Lists agent thread messages.
get.description:
Lists messages from the specified personal-agent or custom-agent conversation.
            Use this endpoint to retrieve replies after creating a thread or submitting a message.
            Returns not found if the thread is missing or the user cannot read it.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

post.summary: Submits a message to an agent conversation.
post.description:
Submits a new message to an existing agent conversation for processing.
            Provide text, attachments, or both. The message starts processing or enters the thread's queue.
            The response confirms acceptance; it does not contain the agent's reply.
            Read [GET /agents/threads/{threadId}/messages](api:GET/agents/threads/{threadId}/messages) to retrieve replies.
            Each request submits a new message. Retrying after a lost response can submit the message again.
            Processing is subject to the workspace's AI availability and usage limits.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have permission to contribute to the thread.</Check>

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.description: The id of the thread to send the message in.

requestBody.description: The model with the content to send to the agent thread.

get.summary: Gets agent thread message status.
get.description:
Returns the processing status of a submitted agent thread message, including messages still in the queue.
            Use the accepted message id returned by the server when creating a thread or submitting a message.
            The response indicates whether an agent response exists and includes its id and error details when available.
            Retrieve reply content with [GET /agents/threads/{threadId}/messages](api:GET/agents/threads/{threadId}/messages).

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

parameters.name: threadId
parameters.description: The id of the thread that contains the message.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The accepted message id returned by the server.

get.summary: Returns the custom agent's configuration.
get.description:
Returns the specified custom agent's configuration, including the requesting user's access level.
            Use this response to inspect the agent's model, prompt, and linked capabilities before working with it.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have read access to the agent.</Check>

put.summary: Updates the custom agent's configuration.
put.description:
Updates the custom agent's configuration and returns the saved agent.
            Saves a new system prompt version if the prompt changes.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have manage access to the agent. Changing workspace sharing also requires permission to contribute to the agent library.</Check>

requestBody.description: The new agent configuration.

delete.summary: Unlinks a connector from an agent.
delete.description:
Removes the connector link from the specified agent.
            Returns no content when the link is removed or is already absent.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have manage access to the agent.</Check>

post.summary: Links a connector to an agent.
post.description:
Links an existing connector to the specified agent and returns the linked connector.
            Use [GET /agents/connectors](#/AgentRuntime/GetConnectors) to find a connector id.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have manage access to the agent.</Check>

post.summary: Copies an existing custom agent.
post.description:
Creates a copy of an existing custom agent in the current workspace.
            Provide the new name and optional description in the request body. The source agent supplies the initial configuration and system prompt.
            Returns the new agent with its own id.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have read access to the source agent.</Check>

requestBody.description: The name and description for the copy.

get.summary: Returns all files of the specified agent.
get.description: <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

post.summary: Creates a file from an upload id.
post.description:
After a file has been uploaded to an upload URL generated from the <see cref="T:Awork.Files.Service.Feature.FileUpload.Endpoints.PostGenerateUploadURL" /> endpoint, this endpoint can be used to create a file agent from the uploaded file by providing the upload id.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

parameters.name: agentId
parameters.description: The id of the agent to attach the file to.

requestBody.description: The model describing the uploaded file metadata.

delete.summary: Deletes the specified agent file and its versions.
delete.description: <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

get.summary: Lists agent schedules.
get.description:
Lists the schedules configured for an agent after checking the caller's read access.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

post.summary: Creates an agent schedule.
post.description:
Creates a schedule for an agent after validating its cadence, timezone, and optional project or task context.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

requestBody.description: The schedule payload.

post.summary: Previews a schedule occurrence.
post.description:
Calculates the next occurrence for the supplied cadence without changing the schedule.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

requestBody.description: The cadence preview request.

delete.summary: Deletes an agent schedule.
delete.description:
Deletes a schedule configured for an agent after checking the caller's access.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

put.summary: Updates an agent schedule.
put.description:
Updates a schedule configured for an agent after validating its cadence, timezone, and optional context.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

requestBody.description: The updated schedule payload.

post.summary: Runs an agent schedule.
post.description:
Immediately starts a new agent session for the selected schedule.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

post.summary: Changes schedule state.
post.description:
Enables or disables the selected agent schedule and returns the updated schedule.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

requestBody.description: The requested enabled state.

post.summary: Archives or unarchives an agent.
post.description:
Archives or unarchives the specified custom agent and returns its updated configuration.
            Set IsArchived to true to archive the agent, or false to unarchive it.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have manage access to the agent.</Check>

requestBody.description: Whether to archive or unarchive the agent.

get.summary: Lists agent skills.
get.description:
Returns the skills linked to an agent after checking read access to the agent.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

post.summary: Creates a private skill for an agent.
post.description:
Creates a private skill owned by the agent and links the new skill to that agent.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

requestBody.description: The name and content of the new skill.

delete.summary: Removes a skill from an agent.
delete.description:
Also deletes the skill if it is private to the agent.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

post.summary: Links a skill to an agent.
post.description:
Links a shared skill to an agent when the caller can manage the agent and read the skill.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

get.summary: Lists the agent's saved system prompt versions.
get.description:
Lists the saved system prompt versions for the specified custom agent.
            Use a returned version id with the system prompt restore endpoint to restore an earlier prompt.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have read access to the agent.</Check>

post.summary: Restores a previous system prompt version.
post.description:
Restores a saved system prompt version as the agent's current prompt.
            The restore records a new history version and returns that version. Use the system prompt versions endpoint to find a version id.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have manage access to the agent.</Check>

get.summary: Returns all API users.
get.description:
Returns API users configured in the workspace.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must be an admin or have `workspace-manage-config:read` permissions.</Check>

post.summary: Creates an API user.
post.description:

get.summary: Returns all documents.
get.description:
Returns documents visible to the current user. Set `includeTrashedDocuments` to include documents in the trash.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have at least `read` permission for each returned document.</Check>

parameters.name: includeTrashedDocuments
parameters.description: Whether to include trashed documents in the result.

post.summary: Creates a document.
post.description:
Creates a document with optional HTML or Markdown content. Set `contentFormat` to `html` or `markdown`; HTML is the default. Canonical awork Markdown preserves safe editor structures during re-import.

<Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">Any authenticated user.</Check>

post.summary: Restores the specified document.
post.description:
Restores the specified document from the trash. Related versions, content, and child documents are restored asynchronously. Restoring an already active document has no effect.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have at least `write` permission for the specified document.</Check>

parameters.name: documentId
parameters.description: The id of the document to restore.

parameters.name: alsoRestoreChildren
parameters.description: Whether to also restore children documents.

delete.summary: Deletes the specified document.
delete.description:
Moves the specified document to the trash. The document is moved synchronously; child documents and related entities are moved asynchronously. Set `alsoDeleteChildren` to control whether child documents are included.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have at least `manage` permission for the specified document.</Check>

parameters.name: documentId
parameters.description: The id of the document to delete.

parameters.name: alsoDeleteChildren
parameters.description: Whether to also delete children documents. If false, the children's parent references are updated to point to the deleted document's parent.

get.summary: Returns the specified document.
get.description:
Returns the specified document when it is visible to the current user.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have at least `read` permission for the specified document.</Check>

parameters.name: documentId
parameters.description: The id of the document to retrieve.

put.summary: Updates the specified document.
put.description:
Updates the specified document's content, location, sharing, or display properties. Moving a document can change its access rules and may be restricted by the workspace plan.
            <Check title="Required Permissions" icon="key">The user must have at least `write` permission for the specified document.</Check>

ComputedValueKind.description:
The kind of computed value in the context of a Awork.Core.Models.Filters.FilterDefinition.Condition.Value.FilterValue.
These represent actual VALUES that can be used with operators (e.g., "dueOn eq today", "dueOn ge sow").
Note: WithinThisWeek and WithinThisMonth are operators (Operator enum), not values.

field.description:
The field to filter on.
For collection fields, use the full path including the inner field (e.g., "tags/id", "assignees/id").

values.description:
The values for this condition. Usage depends on operator:
- Single-value operators (Equal, NotEqual, etc.): Use Values[0]
- Multi-value operators (In): Use all Values
- Range operators (Between): Use Values[0] as start, Values[1] as end
- No-value operators (IsSet, IsNotSet, WithinThisWeek, WithinThisMonth): Values is null or empty

Condition.description:
A condition of a Awork.Core.Models.Filters.FilterDefinition.FilterDefinition, is always part of a Awork.Core.Models.Filters.FilterDefinition.ConditionGroup.
            
conditions can be either:
- Comparison conditions (Type = ConditionType.Comparison): Simple field comparisons like "name eq 'John'"
- Collection conditions (Type = ConditionType.Collection): Collection operations like "tags/any(t: t/name eq 'urgent')"
            
For collection conditions:
- Field contains the full path including inner field (e.g., "tags/name", "assignees/firstName")
- The collection path is extracted from Field (everything before the last '/')

tags.name: Agent Schedules
tags.description: Create, manage, preview, and run schedules for accessible agents.

tags.name: Agent Skills
tags.description: Create and manage reusable skills, sharing, support files, access requirements, and secret values.

tags.name: AgentRuntime
tags.description: Sandbox-backed generic agent runtime endpoints.

tags.name: AgentThreads
tags.description: Manages agent threads.

tags.name: Custom Agents
tags.description: Create and configure custom agents, sharing, skills, connectors, delegations, workflows, and presets.

tags.name: Accounts
tags.description: The accounts endpoints allow you to manage the basic account details of a user.

tags.name: Client Applications
tags.description: Client applications are used by external login flows and workspace-registered applications.

tags.name: AbsenceRegions
tags.description:
An absence region can be used to define the country/region where the employee is working and as such is subject to the labor laws of that country/region.
                    This will define the public holidays entitlements for employees. Can be used to define regional workspace absences as well.

tags.name: Absences
tags.description: The absence endpoints allow you to manage absences for users.

tags.name: ApiUsers
tags.description: API users are required to create API keys. Changes made by an API client are shown in the UI as the respective API user.

tags.name: AssignedTasks
tags.description:
The assigned tasks endpoints allow you to get all assigned tasks of a user.
                    Project tasks are only visible if the related project is in progress.

tags.name: ChecklistItems
tags.description: The checklist items endpoints can be used for managing the checklist items of a task.

tags.name: Companies
tags.description: The company endpoints allow you to add and manage companies and their details.

tags.name: CompanyTags
tags.description: Manage tags for companies.

tags.name: CustomFields
tags.description:
Custom fields are used to extend tasks and projects with additional information.
        They can be used to store additional information. Those are the shared endpoints to work with custom field definitions.

tags.name: Dashboards
tags.description: The dashboards endpoints allow you to work with user's dashboards.

tags.name: DocumentSpaces
tags.description: The document spaces endpoints allow you to create and manage document spaces and related entities such as contributors or connected teams.

tags.name: Documents
tags.description: The documents endpoints allow you to create and manage documents, their versions and related entities such as contributors or connected teams.

tags.name: Filters
tags.description: Provides endpoints to manage and share saved filters.

tags.name: Permissions
tags.description:
The permissions endpoints provide the permission information of the workspace.
                    That includes the complete permission set of the currently logged-in user as well as all available features.

tags.name: PrivateTasks
tags.description:
Private tasks belong to a single user.
                     Only the users themselves have access to their tasks and they can only be assigned to them.
                     It is possible to create and assign private tasks to another user in which case both users have access to the task.

tags.name: ProjectMembers
tags.description: Project Members feature allows you to manage the members of a project, including adding users, assigning roles, and setting responsible members. Only users with the appropriate permissions can add or modify project members. Roles and responsibilities are enforced according to project type and permissions.

tags.name: ProjectMilestoneTemplates
tags.description: The project milestone template endpoints allow you to work with milestone templates for project templates.

tags.name: ProjectMilestones
tags.description: The project milestone endpoints allow you to work with the basic project milestone data.

tags.name: ProjectRoles
tags.description:
The project roles endpoints allow you to define roles for your project members.
                                   You can assign members to these roles on each project.
                                   If the roles are linked to the project types then the roles are available in every project using this type.
                                   When you want to delete a project role which is still in use, you are required to specify which role the currently assigned members should be assigned to instead.

tags.name: ProjectStatuses
tags.description: Manage project and project template statuses.

tags.name: ProjectTags
tags.description: Manage tags for projects.

tags.name: ProjectTasks
tags.description:
The project tasks are linked to projects.
                            Only members of the project or users with project management 'read' permissions have access to these tasks.

tags.name: ProjectTemplateTags
tags.description: Manage tags for project templates.

tags.name: ProjectTemplates
tags.description: The project templates endpoints allow you to define different templates for projects.

tags.name: ProjectTypes
tags.description: The project types endpoints allow you to define different types for projects.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description:
The projects endpoints allow you to work with the basic project data.
                             If you don't assign a customer to the project, the project will be an internal project.
                             In addition to the normal operation you can handle the project members and tags of the projects.
                             When you assign a user to this project as a project member, you need to specify a project role for this project member. The available roles depend on the type of the project.
                             You can also make one member responsible for the project, which means that we will notify this person if anything of interest happens in the project.
                             The tags help you to add additional values to your projects and to find them faster.
                             If you create new tags, they will be available for all other projects, too.

tags.name: Retainers
tags.description: Retainers are used for projects with recurring budgets. Currently only hourly based monthly recurring budgets are supported.

tags.name: Roles
tags.description:
The roles endpoints allow you to configure the permissions of users.
            You have the possibility to manage roles and assign users to these roles.

tags.name: TaskBundles
tags.description: Task bundles are reusable templates for task lists, tasks, and assignments that can be added to projects or created from existing project data.

tags.name: TaskDependencies
tags.description:
The TaskDependencies endpoints allow you to get all task dependencies of a project or a task.
                    A task can have multiple predecessors and multiple successors through separate dependency relationships.

tags.name: TaskDependencyTemplates
tags.description: Manage task dependency templates that belong to task bundles.

tags.name: TaskLists
tags.description:
Task lists are a way to group tasks into user-defined lists.
                            Task lists are currently available in projects and for users.
                            This way, each project and each user can have a set of ordered task lists.
                            Task lists can be reordered as well as the tasks within the list.
                            Since tasks can be in multiple lists, the order is only applied to one list and does not affect others.

tags.name: TaskStatuses
tags.description: The Task statuses endpoints can be used for general task status operation. Only for internal purposes.

tags.name: TaskTags
tags.description: Manage tags for tasks.

tags.name: TaskTemplateTags
tags.description: Manage tags for task templates.

tags.name: TaskTemplates
tags.description: The task templates endpoints can be used for managing task templates within task bundles.

tags.name: Tasks
tags.description:
The Tasks endpoints can be used for general task operations and batch operations.
        The batch operations include changing the task status, assigning users and more.

tags.name: Teams
tags.description: The teams endpoints are used to manage the details of your team.

tags.name: TimeBookings
tags.description:
The time bookings are used as a simple way to book a user's time for a specific time frame.
It can be related to a project or not.
Those bookings are then used in the workload to calculate the estimated load of a user.

tags.name: TimeEntries
tags.description:
There are some endpoints which have a V2 version. For those the V1 endpoints will be deprecated in the future.
                    Please use the V2 endpoints instead.
                    The endpoints can be used for general operations on existing time entries.
                    A time entry can be linked to a task and / or project, although it can also be created for the user themselves without any entity link.
                    If the time entry is linked to a project it is also indirectly linked to the company of that project.
                    Similarly, the time entry is automatically linked to the project of the the task.

tags.name: TimeReports
tags.description: Endpoints for generating and managing time report KPIs and configurations.

tags.name: TimeTracking
tags.description:
The v1 versions of these endpoints will be deprecated at some point. Please migrate to the V2 versions.
                These endpoints can be used to start, stop, pause or resume a time tracking as well as to get the last time tracking of a user.

tags.name: TimeTrackingSettings
tags.description: These endpoints can be used to manage global timetracking settings for a workspace.

tags.name: TypeOfWork
tags.description: The type of work endpoints allow you to manage your types of work. They are helpful to describe the type of a task or a time entry.

tags.name: UserCapacities
tags.description: The user capacity endpoints allow you to define the work capacity of users.

tags.name: UserTags
tags.description: The user tags endpoints allow you to manage tags on users.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: The users endpoints allow you to manage the users of your workspace as well as their contact details.

tags.name: Workflows
tags.description: The workflows endpoints allow you to define and manage workflows for projects and project templates.

tags.name: WorkspaceAbsences
tags.description:
Use those endpoints to define workspace wide absences. A WorkspaceAbsence is an absence that is applied to all the users of the workspace. 
                  It is useful for defining company specific events/holidays, for example.

tags.name: Agent Thread Files
tags.description: Endpoints for files attached to agent threads.

tags.name: Entity Files
tags.description: Endpoints for files attached to entities.

tags.name: FileUpload
tags.description: These endpoints can be used to upload files to the workspace.

tags.name: Files
tags.description: File export endpoints.

tags.name: Images
tags.description:
The image endpoints are used to upload and download profile images, for example for users, projects and your workspace.
                             These endpoints also allow you to crop and scale the image to the size you need.

tags.name: SharedFiles
tags.description: These file endpoints are used to get shared files and public profile images.

tags.name: Temporary Files
tags.description:
The temporary file endpoints allow you to upload and update files
        that do not have a connection to any entity. The files can be linked to an entity later.
        They don't show up in awork before they are either linked to a file or marked as a global file.
        Only the user who uploaded the file has access to the temporary file.

tags.name: Project Automations
tags.description: Endpoints to manage automations and actions scoped to projects.

tags.name: Project Template Automations
tags.description: Endpoints to manage automations and actions scoped to project templates.

tags.name: Workflow Automations
tags.description: Endpoints to manage automations scoped to workflows.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Endpoints to manage webhook configurations, tests, and external integrations.

tags.name: Autopilot
tags.description: Endpoints to manage awork autopilot settings for projects.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Endpoints for full-text search and search index maintenance.

tags.name: Invitations
tags.description: The invitation endpoints are used to invite users to a workspace. You can invite a new user or an existing user to a workspace. The invitation code is used to identify the workspace and the account to which the user should be linked. The invitation code is encrypted and can only be decrypted by the service. The invitation code is valid for 24 hours.

tags.name: Workspaces
tags.description: The workspaces endpoints are used to manage the details of your workspace.
